answer: Hypothesis: In the meta-regression study dataset, only 1 out of the 18 original Experimental Economics studies (project == 'ee') was conducted in the United Kingdom — a proportion of 1/18 ≈ 0.056, i.e. about 5.6%. The sole UK study (id ee.13, "Deferred compensation in multiperiod labor contracts: an experimental test of Lazear's model", 2011) was also replicated in the UK; the remaining 17 original studies were conducted in the United States (11), Germany (2), Switzerland (2), Australia (1) and Austria (1).

payload.hypothesis: Only 1 out of the 18 original Experimental Economics studies in the replication dataset was conducted in the United Kingdom, a proportion of 1/18 ≈ 0.056 (about 5.6%). The only UK-based original study was the 2011 Lazear deferred-compensation experiment (id ee.13); the other 17 originals were conducted in the United States (11), Germany (2), Switzerland (2), Australia (1) and Austria (1).
payload.workflow: 1) Load data/meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (927 rows). 2) Filter to project == 'ee' (Experimental Economics): 18 rows, all with discipline == 'Economics'. 3) Count rows where experiment_country.o == 'United Kingdom': 1. 4) Proportion = 1 / 18 ≈ 0.0556 (5.56%). Notes: UK appears in the data as a single canonical string 'United Kingdom' (no 'UK'/'England'/'Scotland'/'Great Britain' variants anywhere in the column), so an exact string match is correct. No deduplication needed: the 18 ee rows have 18 unique ids (ee.1–ee.18) and null lab_id/aggregated, i.e. one row per original study (unlike ml1/ml3/rpp, which are lab-level). No missing values in experiment_country.o among ee rows.
